task_title: Enemy projectile telegraph (aim-lock + visual cue + AI dodge)

plan_review.notes: Adversarial review across 4 rounds. Round 1: 8 concerns (5 blocking) - sentinel/recycle collision, cadence change, cancellation coverage, virtual-projectile dodge fidelity, perception gating, debug-radius plumbing, weak determinism coverage, accuracy-roll timing. Rounds 2-4 resolved all + surfaced 2 more: (1) sentinel uses -1 (not 0) written explicitly in spawnBehaviorEnemy set(EnemyBehavior,{telegraphMs: options?.telegraphMs ?? -1}) at every spawn, since clearEntityStores zeroes typed-array slots on every createEntity call not just recycled EIDs; (2) cadence change (cooldown+telegraphMs) accepted as intentional additive consequence documented in ADR, not compensated; (3) 5 cancellation call sites identified in enemyAISystem per-enemy loop; (4) virtual-projectile dodge reads explicit locked telegraphOriginX/Y + telegraphDirX/Y stored once at telegraph start, used identically by render cue, AI dodge math, and actual fire-time spawn (lockedOrigin + lockedDir * MUZZLE_OFFSET) - correctness independent of live-position drift from separation/knockback/unstuck; (5) perception gating via canPerceiveWorldPosition on new telegraph-dodge loop; (6) debug plumbing scoped to bt-ai-provider.ts only, travel-steering.ts confirmed out of scope; (7) determinism tests added; (8) accuracy roll stays at fire-time (accepted trade-off); (9) stuckFrames forced to 0 every frame while telegraphActive===1, tryUnstuckVelocity gated off for whole window; (10) applySeparation skips writing velocity onto a telegraphing eid. Final verdict: approved.

rounds.notes: Single-model pass against the full branch diff. Explicitly verified all 9 contract-correctness points from the review brief (delay resolution, 0ms parity, cancellation coverage, actual-attack-range danger radius, virtual-projectile-vs-real-fire consistency, EID-recycling sentinel, CLI wiring, test genuineness, createTestWorld() 0ms masking risk). No concerns raised. The 2 real bugs below were caught only by the independent multi-model fan-out (see multi_model_review), which is why both stages are required at this apple tier.

Post-open shepherding: GitHub's automated PR-review pass re-ran on each push while driving PR #1196 to merge and surfaced 10 further genuine issues beyond the pre-merge stages above: telegraph movement-freeze timing, an FOV-gate bypass in the AI dodge path, dead-shooter dodge still firing, stale CLI help text, a PhaserBridge dead-shooter render-cue gap, stale doc test counts, an unbounded-range dodge case, a recycled-EID cleanup bug, an FOV-vs-live-position mismatch, and missing coordinate-pinned test coverage. Each was root-caused, fixed with a regression test, verified (typecheck/lint/verify:fast), committed, and the corresponding review thread replied-to + resolved before the next push.

Further post-open pass (after an update-branch merge with main): (1) bt-ai-provider.ts range-gate hard-rejected candidates the real fire pipeline actually lets land on the step it first exceeds maxRange — fixed by clamping to maxReachableFrames instead of rejecting, with 2 new regression tests; (2) the 250ms default telegraph delay required a broad (>10-run) GitHub-Actions win-rate sweep per AGENTS.md rule 15/rule 12 before it could be treated as balance-validated — dispatched weapon-sweep.yml on main (95.6% win rate) vs. this branch (92.2%), both comfortably above the 90% Floor-1 gate, documented in the handoff's new Balance validation section; (3)+(4) two stale ADR passages (visibility-gate description, 0ms-legacy-parity consequences); (5) stale PR-description test counts. All fixed, verified, committed, and threads replied-to + resolved.

Further post-open pass after the round-3 push: (1) a round-1-era test comment and the handoff's retrospective wrongly cited the raw (unused) src/shared/data/weapons.json fireball projectileSpeed of 4.0 as the runtime value, when both the fire path and the AI dodge math actually call getWeaponDef('fireball') (src/shared/weaponDefs.ts), which hardcodes 0.5 — corrected the test-comment drift math (3 frames / 92.8 total, not 0.375/90.175) and rewrote the handoff's Mistakes Made / Opportunities sections to cite the true runtime source; (2) a PhaserBridge.ts comment claiming only the render cue is FOV-gated was stale since round 2 already gated the AI dodge path identically — corrected; (3) a real bug: the telegraph cue's urgency-pulse sine phase used the absolute renderElapsedMs while its frequency also depends on progress, causing a phase-discontinuity flicker in long-running sessions — fixed by phasing on the telegraph's own relative elapsedMs instead, with a new regression test (tests/unit/phaser-bridge.test.ts) asserting identical pulse alpha for two telegraphs at the same relative-elapsed-since-start but very different absolute render-clock values; (4) this ledger itself was flagged as stale (marking 'clean' after a single recorded round despite the PR/handoff documenting several further rounds of real bug-finding) — addressed by adding rounds 2-4 above so the ledger's account matches the actual multi-round review history. All fixed, verified (tsc/eslint/verify:fast/full affected-suite reruns), committed, and threads replied-to + resolved.

Further post-open pass after the round-4 push + an update-branch merge with main: (1) a real bug in bt-ai-provider.ts's telegraphed-shot dodge math — the AI's poll() runs BEFORE world.elapsedMs advances and preSystems run for a step, while the fire-ready check runs AFTER that increment but BEFORE that step's movementSystem, so the raw fractional quotient (remainingMs/DELTA_MS) overcounted the player-movement steps remaining before the shot fires by exactly one; fixed to the discrete count (ceil(remainingMs/DELTA_MS) - 1, clamped at 0), verified empirically with a standalone simulation before touching the code, with a new regression test isolating the one-frame dodge-horizon boundary; (2) no regression test existed for the strict-current-FOV-vs-discovered-tile-memory branch (canCurrentlyPerceiveWorldPosition) in the telegraph dodge path — added one proving a discovered-but-not-currently-visible shooter is not dodged, and the same shooter is dodged once its tile enters live FOV; (3) the handoff's stale 'five tests' phaser-bridge-cue counts (two locations) were still five after round 4's urgency-pulse test raised it to six — corrected to six in both places; (4) this ledger's round-1 multi_model_review note still said the muzzle-offset drift was '~0.375 frames' after round 4 already corrected the figure elsewhere in this file to 3 frames — corrected for consistency; (5) the handoff's balance-sweep write-up attributed weapon win-rate deltas to the enemy being able to 're-aim/adjust' during the telegraph window, contradicting the implemented locked-aim/movement-frozen contract — reworded to describe the deltas as an observed outcome of the telegraph delay itself, without the causal re-aim claim; (6) headless-runner-cli-lib.ts:119 used Number.parseFloat, which accepts malformed values with numeric prefixes (e.g. '250ms' -> 250) instead of rejecting the whole token — fixed to Number(next) so malformed CLI input is properly rejected. All fixed, verified (tsc/eslint/full affected-suite reruns/verify:fast), committed, and threads replied-to + resolved.

Consolidated summary of rounds 6-11 (post-open passes across several update-branch merges with main, including absorbing PR #1197's legacy-Floor1-deaths fix to bt-ai-provider.ts): round 6 fixed an unbounded dodge range-gate clamp; round 7 fixed a genuine off-by-one in the remainingFrames dodge-math formula in bt-ai-provider.ts plus a stale test comment; round 8 fixed CLI help text and a PhaserBridge dead-shooter cue gap; round 9 fixed (a) MainGameScene's catch-up-loop AI re-poll running after the frame/elapsedMs increment for steps>0 (diverged from headless's poll-before-increment order, causing a one-frame dodge-horizon mismatch at high sim speeds) by reordering to poll-before-increment, (b) headless-runner.ts's normalizeEnemyTelegraphMs accepting values whose Math.fround() rounds to Infinity (Float32Array overflow) by rejecting non-finite-after-fround values, (c) a factually-backwards 'priming poll' workaround comment in behavior-tree-ai.test.ts (hasPerceptionData is refreshed before tree.tick() within the same poll() call, so the workaround was unnecessary) by removing it, and (d) clarified in this ledger's multi_model_review stage that it is a one-time PR-open-boundary gate, not per-round; round 10 fixed (a) the round-9 Float32 guard only covering headless-runner.ts's config path while spawnBehaviorEnemy and direct world.enemyTelegraphMs mutation bypassed it, by moving the guard into the true single resolver getEffectiveTelegraphMs in enemyTelegraph.ts, (b) --enemy-telegraph-ms silently falling through to the 250ms default on a missing trailing CLI value instead of erroring, and (c) filed tracking issue #1199 for a pre-existing (non-regression) AI-runner-lab 16x-playback render-cue-skip architectural gap rather than fixing it in-PR; round 11 re-ran the round-3 balance sweep against the final PR head (104926c1) and current main (b61c1bc7, now including #1197) per a reviewer request that the original sweep (run against stale commit 0a0435b3) be re-validated after the round 6/7 AI-behavior fixes and main's #1197 merge — results matched the original sweep within rounding noise (overall delta -3.4% vs original -3.3%), confirming no balance regression from the intervening fixes. All fixed/verified (tsc/eslint/full affected-suite reruns/verify:fast each round), committed across f707360f/104926c1 plus docs-only round-11 update, and every thread replied-to + resolved.

Rounds 12-14, covering (a) issue #1199's fix landing independently as PR #1200 (which duplicated/extended this PR's own telegraph work while fixing the 16x AI-runner-lab render-cue-skip gap) merging into main before this PR, and (b) further reviewer findings against the resulting merge. Round 12: clampToFloat32SafeTelegraphMs only guarded Float32-overflow, not negative values — a negative world.enemyTelegraphMs survived Math.fround unchanged and made isEnemyProjectileTelegraphReady's elapsed>=delayMs check trip on frame one, an effectively-instant fire with no visible telegraph; extended the guard to also require candidateMs>=0 (0 stays a legitimate legacy-parity value), with 3 new regression tests. Round 13: after merging origin/main (PR #1200's telegraphWasActiveThisFrame sticky render-frame flag, resolved as 7 purely-additive conflicts across components.ts/enemyTelegraph.ts/PhaserBridge.ts/headless-runner-cli-lib.ts and their tests — no semantic conflict, both sides extended the same functions in non-overlapping ways), two more reviewer findings landed: (i) no regression test pinned the round-9 catch-up-loop poll-before-clock-increment ordering in MainGameScene.ts — added a source-order assertion matching the file's existing pause/step-accounting test style; (ii) --enemy-telegraph-ms treated a whitespace-only value as missing-but-passing because Number('   ')===0, silently resolving to enemyTelegraphMs:0 (telegraph disabled) instead of erroring — fixed the missing-value check to next.trim()==='' , with a regression test. Round 14: an invalid (Float32-overflow/non-finite) per-mob telegraphMs override short-circuited straight to the hardcoded ENEMY_PROJECTILE.TELEGRAPH_MS constant instead of falling through to a validly-configured world.enemyTelegraphMs, silently breaking the documented mob??world??constant precedence — extracted a shared isFloat32SafeNonNegativeTelegraphMs predicate so an invalid per-mob value now falls through to the world-level branch (itself still sanitized) exactly like the pre-existing -1 unset sentinel and negative-override cases; updated one test's stale expectation and added a full-fallthrough-chain regression test. All fixed/verified (tsc/eslint/full affected-suite reruns/verify:fast each round; seed=42 damage unchanged at 37.15), committed across e5060eba (merge)/879920d1/2640e68f and every thread replied-to + resolved.

Round 15, against the 2640e68f/7e0ce7dc push. One real bug: isFloat32SafeNonNegativeTelegraphMs only rejected Float32-overflow (Math.fround(x) non-finite) and negative values, but a tiny nonzero delay (e.g. 1e-50) is finite and non-negative and survives both checks — Math.fround(1e-50)===0, so once written to the Float32Array-backed telegraphMs/telegraphDelayMs stores it becomes byte-identical to an intentional, legitimate 'legacy: no telegraph' 0 override, silently degrading a configured nonzero delay into immediate-fire behavior. Fixed by extending the shared predicate to reject any nonzero candidate whose Math.fround result is exactly 0 (an explicit 0 still passes); mirrored the same check in headless-runner.ts's normalizeEnemyTelegraphMs (config-time throw) and in combatants.ts's spawnBehaviorEnemy (sanitize the per-mob override to TELEGRAPH_MS_UNSET BEFORE it is ever written to the Float32Array store, since a per-mob value read back out of that store post-write can no longer be distinguished from an explicit 0). Added 3 new regression tests in tests/game/enemy-projectile-telegraph.test.ts (world-level underflow fallback, per-mob underflow fallthrough, and the store-sanitizes-before-write assertion) and 2 in tests/unit/headless-runner-telegraph-ms-validation.test.ts (config-time rejection, and an explicit-0-still-accepted control case). Remaining 11 concerns were documentation staleness, not code bugs: two review-ledger consistency findings (this ledger stopping at round 7/round-11-era content despite rounds 12-14 already being in the diff, and the post_open_scope_note's round range) were already fixed in round 7 above but the corresponding GraphQL threads had not yet been replied-to/resolved (process gap, not a re-finding) — resolved this round; a PR-description test-count drift (16 vs the then-current 24 tests) was likewise already fixed in the PR body but its thread was unresolved — resolved; three ADR findings (docs/knowledge/adr/2026-07-16-enemy-projectile-telegraph.md missing telegraphWasActiveThisFrame from the core-data-model inventory, describing the resolver as literal nullish-coalescing instead of its actual validate-and-fallback contract, and describing the render cue as gated only on telegraphActive instead of telegraphActive-OR-the-sticky-flag) were fixed by updating the ADR to match PR #1200's absorbed sticky-flag implementation and this PR's own resolver semantics; four handoff findings (docs/knowledge/handoffs/2026-07-16-enemy-projectile-telegraph.md's resolver description, renderer summary, and two retrospective test-count/coverage mentions all still describing the pre-round-14/pre-#1200-merge state) were fixed to match the final branch (28 telegraph tests, 7 phaser-bridge tests, sticky-flag coverage, validating-fallback resolver contract). All fixed/verified (tsc/eslint/full affected-suite reruns/verify:fast; seed=42 damage unchanged at 37.15), and every thread replied-to + resolved.

Rounds 16-18, covering the fcf2598e/26d1d049/5e7e40f9 pushes. Round 16: an orphaned JSDoc block in enemyTelegraph.ts (two adjacent /** */ blocks, the first unattached to any symbol) -- merged into one block attached to isFloat32SafeNonNegativeTelegraphMs, docs-only, no logic change. Round 17 (5 findings): (1) the PR title/summary misattributed authorship of the entire telegraph feature to this squash-merge -- confirmed via git diff origin/main...HEAD that PR #1200's earlier squash-merge (branched from a full snapshot of this branch) already carried the resolver, render cue, and AI dodge onto main, so this PR's actual remaining diff is delay-validation hardening + design docs; PR retitled and resummarized to reflect that accurately (not a code/gameplay change). (2) JSDoc for isFloat32SafeNonNegativeTelegraphMs's underflow bullet did not explain that per-mob (Float32Array, collapses at write time, unrecoverable at resolve time) and world-level (plain JS number, caught and falls back to the constant at resolve time, never immediate-fire) have different consequences -- clarified. (3) getEffectiveTelegraphMs's inline comment listed only overflow/non-finite/negative as invalid per-mob cases, omitting Float32-underflow-to-zero -- added. (4) headless-runner.ts's config-time rejection comment/error message inaccurately claimed an underflowing world-level value 'would silently select immediate-fire/legacy behavior', which is untrue (the resolver's own guard catches it and falls back to 250ms) -- reworded to the accurate 'cannot be preserved as configured, would be silently replaced by the default' rationale. (5) a stale test comment in enemy-projectile-telegraph.test.ts still described the removed 'perMob >= 0' implementation instead of isFloat32SafeNonNegativeTelegraphMs -- fixed. Round 18 (2 findings, both docs-accuracy): the ADR's CLI section understated the accepted --enemy-telegraph-ms input contract (said only 'finite/non-negative', omitting that Float32-overflow and Float32-underflow-to-zero values are also rejected) -- expanded; and this ledger entry itself, closing the gap the finding flagged (ledger previously ended at round 8/session-round-15 while the PR description already referenced hardening through session-rounds 16-17). All fixed/verified (tsc/eslint/full affected-suite reruns/verify:fast clean; seed=42 damage unchanged at 37.14999961853027), and every thread replied-to + resolved. Also folded in two conflict-free update-branch merges with main (b6bca40f..9af4fdc9..7003b302, unrelated commits: deploy-baseline-comment targeting, equipment weightLb + encumbrance) with no telegraph-code overlap.

Round 19, against the 86e0381d push. One documentation-accuracy finding: the ADR's "every early-exit path" telegraph-cancellation inventory (in the Fire logic section) only listed tryFireEnemyProjectile()'s own three branches (aggro-not-yet-enabled, player not detectable, out-of-range) and implicitly claimed exhaustiveness, but enemyAISystem also cancels telegraphs on three more branches higher up in the function: no player entity present, an inactive Floor 2 boss encounter, and the shooter entering its post-death DeathTimer linger window (src/game/enemyAISystem.ts:1727-1738, 1773-1789). Fixed by rewording the ADR to explicitly enumerate all six branches and reference enemyAISystem's early-exits generally rather than implying tryFireEnemyProjectile is the sole source. Docs-only; no code or logic change (the cancellation calls themselves already existed and were already covered by tests). Verified via direct code read of the three additional call sites; tsc/eslint/verify:fast all clean, seed=42 damage unchanged at 37.14999961853027.

4-way fan-out (3 code-review models + 1 security-review model, gpt-5.4) against the full branch diff. sonnet: no concerns. security (gpt-5.4): no concerns. codex: 2 concerns — (A) enemyAISystem.ts's playerEid===undefined early-return never called cancelEnemyProjectileTelegraph, unlike every other early-exit branch, risking a stale telegraph; (B) bt-ai-provider.ts's telegraphed-virtual-projectile dodge math used the raw locked telegraphOriginX/Y instead of the muzzle-offset-adjusted spawn point that fireEnemyProjectileFrom() actually fires from, a systematic drift of 3 frames (1.5ft MUZZLE_OFFSET / 0.5ft-per-frame runtime fireball speed). gemini independently found the same finding B, corroborating it. Adjudicator (gpt-5.4, xhigh) re-verified both against source, confirmed BOTH VALID with concrete remedies, and confirmed the render cue (PhaserBridge.ts) should stay as-is (intentionally shows locked body position, not the muzzle point). Both fixes applied: (A) added cancelEnemyProjectileTelegraph() call inside the no-player-branch loop; (B) spawnX/Y now computed with ENEMY_PROJECTILE.MUZZLE_OFFSET applied before relativeX/Y. Two new regression tests added (tests/game/enemy-projectile-telegraph.test.ts and tests/game/behavior-tree-ai.test.ts) that fail if either fix is reverted. Full affected-suite re-run + typecheck/lint/verify:fast all green after the fixes.

multi_model_review.post_open_scope_note: A later shepherding-round review (copilot-pull-request-reviewer) suggested this stage should be re-run against the final diff after every post-open fix round. Per docs/agent-os/policies/review-harness-policy.md, multi_model_review is a one-time PR-open-boundary gate validated by the pr-review-ledger guard at create_pull_request, not a per-push requirement — the policy's own 'Bounded review loop' and 'Enforcement' sections scope it to that boundary. Post-open shepherding rounds are correctly tracked under code_review (which explicitly permits single-model rounds, e.g. copilot-pull-request-reviewer), matching rounds 2-9 above (round 7 is a consolidated summary covering rounds 12-14; round 8 covers round 15).
